artworks.title: The Danaides
artworks.description: Waterhouse's Danaides — the sisters forever pouring into broken jars, Tartarus' punishment for the wedding-night massacre.

artworks.title: The Danaides Killing Their Husbands
artworks.description: The Danaids killing their husbands — the wedding-night slaughter that earns the jars of Tartarus.

artworks.title: Hypermnestra Writing
artworks.description: Hypermnestra writing — the one bride who spares Lynceus, breaking the sisters' bloody pact.

artworks.title: Plate with Hypermnestra Watching Lynceus Take Her Father's Crown
artworks.description: Hypermnestra watches Lynceus escape — the solitary mercy among Danaus' fifty daughters.

artworks.title: The Daughters of Danaus
artworks.description: Sabatté's Daughters of Danaus — the fifty brides whose crime becomes Argos' founding myth and the underworld's sieve.

popCulture.title: Danaïdes
popCulture.description: The fifty sisters who murdered their bridegrooms remain the emblem of endless futile labour — pouring water into a leaking jar in the underworld.
